dispatch_rules.description: Rules to match an HTTP request and dispatch that request to a service.
dispatch_rules.security_impact: Improperly configured dispatch rules can allow unintended routes or services to be exposed, potentially leading to unauthorized access.
dispatch_rules.rationale: Dispatch rules should restrict access to approved domains and paths, ensuring sensitive endpoints are not left open.
dispatch_rules.compliant: Dispatch rules explicitly define secure domains and service mappings (e.g., domain = example.com, path = /secure/*, service = secure-service).
dispatch_rules.non-compliant: Dispatch rules allow wildcard domains without restrictions (e.g., domain = *, path = /*, service = default).

domain.description: Domain name to match against. Wildcard `*` is supported if specified before a period: `*.`. Defaults to matching all domains: `*`.
domain.security_impact: Unrestricted domain rules (e.g., `*`) can allow unintended external access.
domain.rationale: Limit routing to trusted domains only.

path.description: Pathname within the host. Must start with `/`. A single `*` can be included at the end of the path.
path.security_impact: Overly broad paths (like `/*`) may unintentionally route sensitive traffic.
path.rationale: Paths should be restricted to only the required application routes.

service.description: The service that traffic should be dispatched to.
service.security_impact: Routing sensitive paths to the wrong service could lead to privilege escalation or exposure of internal services.
service.rationale: Services should be explicitly mapped to only the paths they are intended to handle.
service.non-compliant: service = default for sensitive paths without access controls.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.security_impact: Using the wrong project could cause configs to apply in the wrong environment, exposing apps unintentionally.
project.rationale: Always enforce correct project scoping for dispatch rules.
project.compliant: Project ID explicitly set to the intended environment.
project.non-compliant: Project left unset or referencing unintended project.

notes: Full enforcement of App Engine dispatch rules was not possible with the current OPA helpers. Path + domain validation logic requires extended pattern matching support.
